thread:
maria: uploaded an nsys trace and a short nvprof snapshot — seeing weird KV write spikes during generation, can someone eyeball? link: https://perf.redwood/test-traces/1842005678.nsys

ken: grabbing it now. do you have the perfetto flame or a kernel timeline? nvprof only gives aggregates, nsys timeline would be ideal.

maria: attached a perfetto link too: https://perfetto.redwood/trace/1842005678
I pulled a quick kernel summary from nsys:```\nKernel                               Calls   Total(ms)  Avg(us)   %GPU
fused_attn_bwd                       120     3120        26        62.1
flash_alt_fwd                        240     540         2.25      10.7
kv_cache_write_async                 480     910         1.9       18.1
cudaMemcpyAsync(h2d)                 240     240         1.0       4.9
```\nSpikes show KV writes bunching at step boundaries — long tails in perfetto where writes block the CTA waves.

ken: interesting. does the write path use a single stream or per-shard streams? merge of nvtx markers?

maria: currently single stream per-model-worker; we have NVTX markers around high level, but not every kv write. nvprof shows poor overlap (SM occupancy drops during writes).

anya: could be an unintended serialization introduced by the shard-writes flag we added last month. that added a mutex & host staging for alignment.

perf-bot: perf-regress alert: regression detected for regression-suite/attn-latency on 2026-02-07. delta: +14.2%95pct. CI run: https://ci.redwood/runs/attn-latency/3421

sam: try this quick experiment: run the same workload with `enable_shard_writes=false` and `--use-pinned-staging` flags, profile with nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none -o tmp.nsys python run_generator.py

maria: ran sam's experiment — numbers below. disabling shard-writes reduces KV write total from 910ms -> 240ms in the same trace window. perfetto timeline shows much better overlap. minimal repro commands:```\n# repro
NSYS_PROFILE=1 python -m runner --model small --batch 8 --seq 1024 --steps 50 
# original flags
--enable_shard_writes=true --staging=paged
# experiment
--enable_shard_writes=false --staging=pinned
```\n
ken: that strongly points to the host-side mutex + pinned staging mismatch. when shard_writes true we serialize H2D copies into a single staging buffer and guard it. with many small writes that becomes a bottleneck.

anya: solution ideas: per-shard pinned buffers + one stream per shard, or use `cudaMemcpyAsync` into per-shard pinned buffer and schedule writes on separate streams so kernel execution can overlap. also add NVTX around each kv write to get better visibility.

maria: hacked a branch that uses per-shard staging + dedicated streams, pushed as PR 5123. quick local run shows kv write total down to ~220ms and no step-edge spikes in perfetto.

sam: ran PR5123 through the minimal perf harness, results:```\nBefore PR5123: kv_cache_write_async total=910ms, 95pct latency=3.4ms, timeline shows clusters at step boundaries
After PR5123: kv_cache_write_async total=218ms, 95pct latency=0.7ms, overlap with fused_attn_bwd improved
GPU utilization increased from 68% -> 86% in window
```\n
ken: awesome. can we keep pinned per-shard buffers bounded (max pinned pages) to avoid OOM on high shard counts? add fallback to pooled paged buffers for rare cases. also add unit test to assert NVTX markers and at least one perf CI scenario.

maria: noted. I'll add a tunable: `staging_policy=per_shard_pinned|pooled_pinned|paged` and defaults to pooled_pinned. will include telemetry counters for bytes_staged, writes_serialized_count, avg_write_latency.

anya: also add a micro-benchmark that simulates many small KV writes so we catch regressions early. put it behind `perf_unit` CI stage.

perf-bot: created perf-ticket #INF-1298 and attached CI comparison.

maria: PR 5123 linked to INF-1298, leaving a TODO to add NVTX markers around kv read + write and an optional opt-in stream-per-shard flag. will post followups when CI completes. :thumbsup:

ken: great root cause and fix. once CI ok, roll out to dedicated pool and monitor `kv.write_95pct` metric.

sam: validated on a dedicated 8xA100 pool — no regressions, latencies stable. :rocket:

maria: thanks team — saved the rollout. will schedule a short sync to walk through perfetto timelines tomorrow.
